newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Bulgaria aid possible when conditions right-EU.
newsitem.headline: New Bulgaria aid possible when conditions right-EU.

text.p: Bulgaria's political stability must be assured before any aid package including accession to international financial bodies can be considered, EU External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Thursday.

Bulgaria's political parties would have to reach consensus on early elections to restore the stability which could lead to the necessary economic reforms, he said after he and Commission President Jacques Santer met Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov.

"Under these normal and traditional conditions the EU is prepared to take initiatives with international financial institutions to see how economic assistance can be mobilised," van den Broek told reporters.
He said in reply to a question on whether the EU would go it alone on a new aid package that it was important that Bulgaria saw eye to eye with the IMF.
The Bulgarian president told NATO ambassadors in Brussels on Wednesday his country faced financial collapse and may have to default on its debt repayments to avoid a social explosion.
He said Bulgaria had not received proper recognition for its sacrifices in complying with international economic embargoes against former Yugoslavia and Iraq.

Stoyanov's Brussels visit came as Bulgarian protesters in Sofia stepped up strikes, rallies and blockades, unmoved by an appeal from the ex-communist ruling Socialists for talks to set an election date.

Bulgaria, its economy in ruins, has been plunged into its worst crisis since the fall of communism in 1989 by 25 days of demonstrations calling for quick elections and an end to rule by the Socialists, who won parliamentary elections in 1994.
